title: Putting Back Excess Withdrawal Fees a Review Found Wrongly Charged
content:
Where a review of an account of Savings & Money Market Accounts finds that excess withdrawal fees were charged against withdrawals that never counted toward the allowance, the fees concerned are put back onto the account as one bank error credit.

The credit is booked against the fee entry whose reference number is given and carries the same fee code as that entry. The account's posted balance rises by the credited amount at once, and the customer sees a bank error credit line dated today against that fee and a balance higher by that amount.

### Recording the credit

The credit is recorded with the tool `credit_savings_fee_review_ce0a6323`. It is an agent-side tool: the agent unlocks it and then calls it. One call posts one bank error credit.

### Parameters

`savings_account_id` — the reference number of the savings or money market account receiving the review credit, taken from the savings account lookup.

`customer_id` — the customer reference number of the account owner, taken from the customer profile lookup.

`source_item_id` — the reference number of the fee entry the review credit is booked against, taken from the savings account activity lookup.

`statement_cycle` — the statement cycle the review credit itself posts in, being the month in which that cycle closes. It is written as YYYY-MM, and an empty value is not accepted.

`review_credit_amount` — the review credit being posted, in USD to 2 decimal places, always positive. A value carrying more than 2 decimal places is stored rounded half up to the cent, and the bank's own Eastern Time posting date is used.

### What the call returns

A confirmation sentence carrying the reference number of the review credit just created, the credited amount in USD to two decimal places, the reference number of the fee entry it is booked against, and the account's new posted balance in USD to two decimal places. That sentence is what indicates the credit completed.
